column1: # Worked-example verdicts for libraries in THIS repo (@PLN141).
# `make libraries-review` names the library.  A library with no `// Example:`
# citation and no row here is TODO — the point of the file is that "nothing here
# teaches more from a call site" and "nobody has looked yet" stop looking alike.
#   exempt   — no function here teaches more from a call site than from its signature.
#   deferred — one does, but not this pass; the reason names what unblocks it, and the
#              monthly review (doc/claude/LIBRARY_DOC_REVIEW.md) is where it comes back.

column3: A fixture, not a shipped library: it exists to be imported by tests/docs/17-libraries.loft and tests/diagnostic_reach.rs, so its `add`/`distance`/`bump` are deliberately trivial and a call site teaches nothing its signature does not.

The IR builder behind lib/parser.loft. Its emitter half (the *_value family, add_block/end_block, add_loop/end_loop, else_if/end_if) has no call site anywhere to cite: parser.loft resolves types and declarations but does not yet emit code. Unblocked when the self-hosting parser emits into Code.

One unfinished function, `convert(dir, into)`, which writes a heading-only page per source file; a call site teaches nothing its signature and doc comment do not. Revisit when it renders the lexed source.
